subject: pathology
title: Fibroadenoma, Phyllodes, Fibrocystic Change, DCIS, and Invasive Breast Carcinomas

steps.tx: Fibroadenoma biphasically grows glands and stroma into rubbery mobile breast mice of young women, enlarging in pregnancy, involuting calcified after menopause, observation or excision by symptoms. That breast mouse is **fibroadenoma of young women**. This point is tested repeatedly because it changes everyday bedside decisions.
steps.say: A rubbery mobile lump in a twenty year old is fibroadenoma; ultrasound and age usually settle it.

steps.tx: Phyllodes tumours leaf stroma into clefts with stromal overgrowth grading benign borderline malignant, haematogenous spread when malignant, axillary nodes characteristically spared. That leafy stromal tumour is **phyllodes tumour of breast**. Examiners return to it because it separates careful clinicians from guesswork. Bedside recognition of this pattern saves time, blood, and unnecessary investigation.
steps.say: Leaf like clefts and stromal overgrowth name phyllodes; grade the stroma, spare the axilla.

vis.alt: Breast cancer surgical anatomy and staging
vis.caption: Breast anatomy and cancer staging framing benign and malignant lump triage.

steps.tx: Fibrocystic change bundles cysts, apocrine metaplasia, fibrosis, and usual ductal hyperplasia of fluctuating premenopausal breasts, malignancy risk only when atypical hyperplasia joins. That risk split is **fibrocystic change and atypical hyperplasia**. Students should anchor this fact before moving to rarer causes and exceptions.
steps.say: Fibrocystic change reassures; atypical hyperplasia inside it is the finding that changes surveillance.

steps.tx: Intraductal papilloma arborescences fibrovascular stalks into ducts causing bloody nipple discharge, peripheral multiple papillomas carrying more atypia and cancer association than solitary central ones. That discharge source is **intraductal papilloma of breast**. In practice this distinction decides the next test, treatment, or referral made.
steps.say: Single duct bloody discharge thinks central papilloma first; excise to exclude its atypical neighbours.

steps.tx: Ductal carcinoma in situ fills ducts with malignant epithelium behind basement membrane, mammographic calcifications its herald, grades and necrosis scheduling excision radiation endocrine decisions. That preinvasive disease is **ductal carcinoma in situ (DCIS)**. That is why this detail earns its place in every examination and ward round.
steps.say: Calcifications without a lump may be DCIS; grade and margins decide its surgery and radiation.

vis.caption: Breast cancer subtypes and metastatic patterns beyond DCIS.

steps.tx: Invasive ductal carcinoma, no special type, forms glands and desmoplastic masses commonest among breast cancers, while medullary mucinous tubular special types refine prognosis. The common mass is **invasive ductal carcinoma (NST)**. Remembering it prevents the commonest errors made with this presentation entirely.
steps.say: Most breast cancers are invasive ductal NST; special types earn their names by kinder prognoses.

steps.tx: Invasive lobular carcinoma loses E-cadherin adhering protein, infiltrating single file without desmoplasia, hiding from mammography, bilateral and multifocal more often. That discohesion is **E-cadherin loss in invasive lobular carcinoma**. The clinical payoff comes from applying it early, before complications accumulate further. This point is tested repeatedly because it changes everyday bedside decisions.
steps.say: Single file cells without E-cadherin hide lobular cancer from mammograms; MRI finds its extent.

steps.tx: Triple assessment, examination imaging and core pathology concordantly, governs every breast lump, discordance forcing excision because cancers hide behind benign single opinions. That concordance law is **triple assessment of breast lumps**. Examiners return to it because it separates careful clinicians from guesswork.
steps.say: Examination, imaging, and core must agree; any discordant leg sends the lump to excision.
